routes.label: Tangent lengths and a right triangle

question:
In the adjoining figure \(TP\) and \(T'Q\) are parallel tangents to a circle of radius \(r,\) with \(T\) and \(T'\) the points of tangency. \(PT''Q\) is a third tangent with \(T''\) as point of tangency. If \(TP=4\) and \(T'Q=9\) then \(r\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1974_AMC_12_Q23_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The third tangent lets us find \(PQ\): tangent segments from the same external point have equal lengths. Thus
\[
PT''=PT=4,\qquad QT''=QT'=9.
\]
The figure places \(T''\) between \(P\) and \(Q\), so \(PQ=4+9=13\).

A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent. Since the tangents at \(T\) and \(T'\) are distinct and parallel, their perpendicular radii lie on the same diameter. Consequently \(TT'=2r\).

Drop a perpendicular from \(P\) to the lower tangent, meeting it at \(H\). The quadrilateral \(TPHT'\) is a rectangle, so \(PH=TT'=2r\) and \(T'H=TP=4\). Since \(T'Q=9\), we have \(HQ=9-4=5\). Right triangle \(PHQ\) therefore gives
\[
(2r)^2+5^2=13^2,
\qquad 4r^2=144,
\qquad r^2=36.
\]
A radius is positive, so \(\boxed{r=6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Joining the external points to the center reveals another useful feature: the center lies on the bisector of the angle between the two tangents from each point. Hence \(OP\) bisects \(\angle TPQ\), and \(OQ\) bisects \(\angle T'QP\).

Because \(PT\) and \(QT'\) are parallel rays pointing in the same direction, the angles they make with the opposite rays \(PQ\) and \(QP\) are supplementary. Therefore
\[
\angle OPQ+\angle OQP
=\frac12(180^\circ)=90^\circ.
\]
The angle sum in triangle \(POQ\) now gives \(\angle POQ=90^\circ\).

The radius \(OT''\) is perpendicular to the tangent \(PQ\). Thus it is the altitude from the right angle of triangle \(POQ\) to its hypotenuse. Write \(X=T''\). Equal tangent lengths give \(PX=4\), \(QX=9\), and \(OX=r\).

Right triangles \(PXO\) and \(OXQ\) are similar: both have a right angle at \(X\), and \(\angle XPO=\angle XOQ\), since each is complementary to \(\angle OQP\). Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{PX}{OX}=\frac{OX}{XQ},
\qquad \frac4r=\frac r9.
\]
Since \(r>0\), cross-multiplication is valid and gives \(r^2=36\). Therefore \(\boxed{r=6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Tangent angle bisectors and similarity
